qualifying_findings.title: OpenAI updated its public Hugging Face model-evaluation incident report with exploitation scope and hardening details
qualifying_findings.summary: OpenAI's July 28 update says attackers exploited a Hugging Face Artifactory zero-day to run code during a third-party evaluation, generated unusual token volume, created nearly 17,600 actions, and accessed four OpenAI accounts. OpenAI says exposed data included public model evaluation artifacts and some credentials, while customer API keys, ChatGPT data, production services, model weights, and source code were not impacted. The update names mitigations including identity-token revocation, credential rotation, token control review, audit-log review, and additional monitoring.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary incident update plus reputable secondary report
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Third-party Hugging Face model-evaluation environment; OpenAI evaluation artifacts and limited account credentials; Modal Labs also reported exposure per Axios.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI model evaluation pipelines are supply-chain and data-exposure boundaries; third-party sandbox escape, credential exposure, and artifact access need explicit isolation, token minimization, and incident evidence gates.

upstream_routing.note: Provider/entity context belongs upstream; keep incident and mitigation lens locally.
Platform/entity context belongs upstream; keep third-party evaluation supply-chain incident locally.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for OpenAI facts from primary update; Modal Labs exposure is carried as secondary-report context only.
follow_up_actions: In ingest, reconcile with existing incident-response/openai-hugging-face-cyber-evaluation-incident.md and update only if the July 28 delta is not already captured.
Watch for Hugging Face or Modal postmortem updates before treating secondary-reported scope as final.

qualifying_findings.title: Hugging Face published a technical timeline for the cyber-evaluation environment compromise
qualifying_findings.summary: Hugging Face's technical report says the incident chain began with an Artifactory zero-day that gave unauthorized access to an environment used for partner evaluation workloads. The report describes access to HDF5 model-configuration data, Jinja2 template execution risk, Kubernetes service-account credential exposure, lateral movement attempts, and cleanup actions such as revoking tokens, rotating secrets, and rebuilding infrastructure.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Hugging Face evaluation infrastructure and partner cyber-evaluation workloads; HDF5/Jinja2 evaluation artifacts and Kubernetes credentials are named affected boundaries.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The report gives reproducible threat-model detail for evaluation sandboxes: model artifacts and templates can become execution surfaces, and evaluation infrastructure needs secret isolation, ephemeral credentials, and strong workload containment.

upstream_routing.note: Broad platform page belongs upstream; local page should keep only evaluation-infrastructure security lessons.
General template-engine entity is upstream; local security lens is prompt/model-artifact execution risk.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence; primary source supplies publication date and concrete incident facts.

qualifying_findings.title: Google Cloud Monitoring MCP documentation was updated with Model Armor checks for AI-generated insights
qualifying_findings.summary: The Cloud Monitoring MCP documentation says natural-language responses are checked with Model Armor when the MCP server is enabled, and names filter categories including prompt injection, malicious URL, sensitive data, sexually explicit, dangerous content, harassment, hate speech, and Cloud Logging IAM-aware response controls.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Google Cloud Monitoring MCP server responses and Cloud Logging queries; Model Armor and IAM-aware response controls.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Observability agents can expose sensitive logs or act on untrusted natural-language context; this page documents a concrete runtime filtering and IAM-control boundary for AI-generated operational insights.

qualifying_findings.summary: Google Cloud's MCP AI security and safety page describes IAM allow and deny policies that can control which Google Cloud MCP tools are available to users or groups through the tool.name permission, along with audit logging and least-privilege practices for agent access.

qualifying_findings.summary: The Google Cloud MCP release notes, visibly updated July 27, include a July 22 entry that fixes an issue in which the Cursor OAuth redirect URI was not supported during configuration setup.

qualifying_findings.title: MCP Go SDK v1.7.0 added support for the 2026-07-28 protocol revision and new HTTP header handling
qualifying_findings.summary: The MCP Go SDK v1.7.0 release says it supports protocol version 2026-07-28, switches streamable HTTP server sessions to stateless by default, adds request and response header support, adds server discovery, deprecates the older header hook path, and removes the deprecated sse package.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk v1.7.0; MCP protocol 2026-07-28; streamable HTTP sessions; header handling; server discovery.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP SDK transport defaults, header propagation, server discovery, and deprecated-package removal affect authentication, session management, gateway mediation, audit headers, and supply-chain upgrade planning for AI tools.

upstream_routing.note: Protocol overview belongs upstream; security-specific transport and auth implications belong locally.
SDK entity belongs upstream; local capture should focus on security-relevant version delta.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for release date and version delta from GitHub release page; security impact is an inference from transport and header-handling changes.

qualifying_findings.title: Singapore CSA and IMDA published an advisory on safe and secure use of generative AI
qualifying_findings.summary: Singapore's Cyber Security Agency and Infocomm Media Development Authority issued Advisory AD-2026-008 for safe and secure use of generative AI. The advisory warns users not to submit sensitive or personal information unless necessary and permitted, to verify AI outputs before acting on them, to review third-party GenAI app permissions, and to use secure configurations and organizational controls.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Generative AI user, organizational, and third-party application usage; data disclosure and app-permission boundaries.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The advisory is a public governance and risk-management signal that treats GenAI data entry, third-party app permissions, and output verification as concrete security controls rather than optional usage tips.

upstream_routing.note: Broad technology overview belongs upstream; local page owns security guidance and controls.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence; primary government advisory has an in-window visible date and security guidance.
follow_up_actions: Route governance controls locally; avoid duplicating general GenAI explanation from ai-wiki.

qualifying_findings.title: Microsoft disclosed Project Perception and MAI-Cyber-1-Flash cyber-evaluation results in public reporting
qualifying_findings.summary: Public reporting says Microsoft introduced Project Perception, a benchmark meant to measure how AI systems perform on cyber tasks, and MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, a model reportedly able to complete a meaningful share of simulated cyberattack tasks while being limited to internal Microsoft Security use with human sign-off requirements.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: reputable secondary reporting; official primary source not found during this run
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Microsoft Project Perception benchmark and MAI-Cyber-1-Flash cyber model; internal Microsoft Security deployment boundary per reports.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Cyber-capable AI evaluation and restricted internal deployment controls are concrete assurance and release-gate signals for dual-use models; the item also illustrates why model capability reporting needs source quality and access-boundary notes.

upstream_routing.note: Provider and model-family coverage belongs upstream; local capture should focus on cyber-evaluation and release-gate implications.
Benchmark entity may belong upstream; security-assurance implications belong locally.
